```{r setup, include=FALSE}
format_glm_equation <- function(fit, digits = 3, proper_names=NULL) {
  b <- coef(fit)
  terms <- names(b)
  parts <- character(length(b))
  for (i in seq_along(b)) {
    if(!is.null(proper_names)) {
      terms[i]<-proper_names[i]
    }
    val <- round(b[i], digits)
    if (terms[i] == "(Intercept)") {
      parts[i] <- format(val, nsmall = digits)
    } else {
      sign <- if (val >= 0) " + " else " - "
      parts[i] <- paste0(sign, format(abs(val), nsmall=digits), ifelse(nchar(terms[i])>0, paste0("[", terms[i], "]"),""))
    }
  }
  paste0(parts, collapse = "")
}


# --- Execution parameters ---

  # glmnet folds, MCMC draws). It is part of the run signature, so changing it

  seed = 123,

  logf_m = 2,
```

## Data wrangling
```{r tab-desc-data, echo = FALSE, include = FALSE}
set.seed(settings$seed)
data(gusto)
df  <- gusto

# Build predictor variables
df$Y  <- gusto$day30
df$X0 <- (df$sex == "female") * 1
df$X1 <- df$age
df$X2 <- (df$miloc == "Other") * 1
df$X3 <- (df$miloc == "Anterior") * 1
df$X4 <- (df$pmi == "yes") * 1
df$X5 <- as.numeric(df$Killip) - 1
df$X6 <- pmin(df$sysbp, 100)
df$X7 <- df$pulse
df$population <- df$regl
df <- df[order(df$regl), c("X1", "X2", "X3", "X4", "X5", "X6", "X7", "Y", "population")]
df$intercept <- 1
df_final  <- df
df_sample <- df_final[sample(nrow(df_final), 500), ]



# Per-variable summary line builders.
fmt_continuous <- function(x) {
  m <- mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  s <- sd(x,   na.rm = TRUE)
  sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", m, s)
}
fmt_binary <- function(x) {
  n_yes <- sum(x == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  n_tot <- sum(!is.na(x))
  sprintf("%d (%.1f)", n_yes, 100 * n_yes / n_tot)
}
fmt_ordinal <- function(x) {
  med <- median(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  q1  <- quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)
  q3  <- quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)
  sprintf("%g (%g, %g)", med, q1, q3)
}
fmt_levels <- function(x, level_labels = NULL) {
  tab <- table(x)
  total <- sum(tab)
  lvl_names <- if (is.null(level_labels)) names(tab) else level_labels[names(tab)]
  paste(
    sprintf("%s: %d (%.1f%%)", lvl_names, tab, 100 * tab / total),
    collapse = "; "
  )
}

# Build one row per variable.
desc_rows <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(settings$var_specs)), function(i) {
  v <- df_final[[settings$var_specs$key[i]]]
  switch(settings$var_specs$type[i],
         continuous = fmt_continuous(v),
         binary     = fmt_binary(v),
         ordinal    = fmt_ordinal(v),
         levels     = fmt_levels(v, level_labels = c("0" = "I", "1" = "II",
                                                     "2" = "III", "3" = "IV")))
}, character(1))

desc_df <- data.frame(
  Variable = settings$var_specs$name,
  Summary  = desc_rows,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names = FALSE

  n_events   = sum(df_final$Y == 1),
  prevalence = mean(df_final$Y)
), file = paste0(res_dir, "table_gusto_desc.rds"))
```

## Make models, their predictions and add them to df_sample and Doe
```{r}
set.seed(settings$seed)

X <- model.matrix(settings$fm_model, df_sample)

# ---- Flat prior ----
reg_f <- glm(settings$fm_model, data = df_sample, family = binomial())
gusto_collector$models$reg_f$eq <- format_glm_equation(reg_f, proper_names=c("", settings$var_specs$short_name))
gusto_collector$models$reg_f$coefs <- summary(reg_f)$coefficients[,1:2]
tmp <- predict(reg_f, se.fit = TRUE)
df_sample$pred_pe_f <- plogis(tmp$fit)
df_sample$pred_pm_f <- predict_pm(X, coef(reg_f), vcov(reg_f))


gusto_collector$Doe$pred_f$pe <- plogis(coef(reg_f) %*% settings$Doe)
tmp <- predict_pm(t(settings$Doe), coef(reg_f), vcov(reg_f), return_sd = T)
gusto_collector$Doe$pred_f$pm <- tmp$pi
gusto_collector$Doe$pred_f$cri <- plogis(c(qlogis(gusto_collector$Doe$pred_f$pe)) + c(-1.96, 1.96) * tmp$sd_eta)
s <- gusto_collector$models$reg_f$eq
for(i in seq_along(settings$Doe[-1])) {
    s <- gsub(
        paste0("\\[X", i, "\\]"),
        paste0("*", settings$Doe[i + 1]),
        s
    )
}
gusto_collector$Doe$eq <- s

# ---- Self-projection of flat-prior PM ----
reg_f_pp <- glm.fit(X, df_sample$pred_pm_f, family = binomial())
df_sample$pred_pm_f_pp <- plogis(X %*% reg_f_pp$coefficients)
gusto_collector$models$reg_f_pp$coefs <- reg_f_pp$coefficients
gusto_collector$Doe$pred_f$pp <- plogis(settings$Doe %*% reg_f_pp$coefficients)


# ---- Jeffreys prior ----
reg_j <- update(reg_f, method = "brglmFit", type = "AS_mean")
gusto_collector$models$reg_j$coefs <- summary(reg_j)$coefficients[,1:2]
tmp <- predict(reg_j, se.fit = TRUE)
df_sample$pred_pe_j    <- plogis(tmp$fit)
df_sample$pred_pm_j    <- predict_pm(X, coef(reg_j), vcov(reg_j))
df_sample$pred_pm_j_mk <- elogitnorm(tmp$fit, tmp$se.fit, "mackay")

gusto_collector$Doe$pred_j$pe <- plogis(coef(reg_j) %*% settings$Doe)
tmp <- predict_pm(t(settings$Doe), coef(reg_j), vcov(reg_j), return_sd = T)
gusto_collector$Doe$pred_j$pm <- tmp$pi
gusto_collector$Doe$pred_j$pm_mk <- predict_pm(t(settings$Doe), coef(reg_j), vcov(reg_j), "mackay")
gusto_collector$Doe$pred_j$cri <- plogis(c(qlogis(gusto_collector$Doe$pred_j$pe)) + c(-1.96, 1.96) * tmp$sd_eta)


# ---- log-F(2,2) prior ----
reg_lf <- logf_glm(X, df_sample$Y)
df_sample$pred_pm_lf <- predict_pm(X, reg_lf$coefficients, reg_lf$vcov)
gusto_collector$models$reg_lf$coefs <- cbind(estimates = reg_lf$coefficients, SE = reg_lf$se)

gusto_collector$Doe$pred_lf$pe <- plogis(reg_lf$coefficients %*% settings$Doe)
tmp <- predict_pm(t(settings$Doe), reg_lf$coefficients, reg_lf$vcov, return_sd = T)
gusto_collector$Doe$pred_lf$pm <- tmp$pi
gusto_collector$Doe$pred_lf$cri <- plogis(c(qlogis(gusto_collector$Doe$pred_lf$pe)) + c(-1.96, 1.96) * tmp$sd_eta)


# ---- Bayesian Ridge ----
reg_br <- bayesian_ridge(X, df_sample$Y)
df_sample$pred_pm_br <- predict_pm(X, reg_br$beta, reg_br$V)
gusto_collector$models$reg_br$coefs <- cbind(estimate = reg_br$beta, SE = sqrt(diag(reg_br$V)))

gusto_collector$Doe$pred_br$pe <- plogis(settings$Doe %*% reg_br$beta)
tmp <- predict_pm(t(settings$Doe), reg_br$beta, reg_br$V, return_sd = T)
gusto_collector$Doe$pred_br$pm <- tmp$pi
gusto_collector$Doe$pred_br$pm_mk <- predict_pm(t(settings$Doe), reg_br$beta, reg_br$V, method = "mackay")
gusto_collector$Doe$pred_br$cri <- plogis(c(qlogis(gusto_collector$Doe$pred_br$pe)) + c(-1.96, 1.96) * tmp$sd_eta)


# ---- Self-projection PM (and complete MacKay PM) for Sam Doe, all Laplace priors ----
# Self-projection: regress the prior's posterior-mean soft-labels on the design
# matrix, then predict Sam Doe; MacKay is the closed-form logit-normal mean.
doe_x <- t(settings$Doe)
.self_proj_doe <- function(pm_soft) {
  fit_pp <- suppressWarnings(glm.fit(X, pm_soft, family = binomial()))
  as.numeric(plogis(settings$Doe %*% fit_pp$coefficients))
}
# Flat
gusto_collector$Doe$pred_f$pm_mk  <- predict_pm(doe_x, coef(reg_f),  vcov(reg_f),  "mackay")
gusto_collector$Doe$pred_f$pm_pp  <- .self_proj_doe(df_sample$pred_pm_f)
# Jeffreys
gusto_collector$Doe$pred_j$pm_pp  <- .self_proj_doe(df_sample$pred_pm_j)
# log-F(2,2)
gusto_collector$Doe$pred_lf$pm_mk <- predict_pm(doe_x, reg_lf$coefficients, reg_lf$vcov, "mackay")
gusto_collector$Doe$pred_lf$pm_pp <- .self_proj_doe(df_sample$pred_pm_lf)
# Bayesian ridge
gusto_collector$Doe$pred_br$pm_pp <- .self_proj_doe(df_sample$pred_pm_br)


# ---- MCMC Bayesian Ridge (exact, no-Laplace reference) ----
# Fit the hand-written Stan ridge on the development sample, then summarise the
# posterior on the ORIGINAL coefficient scale (back-transformed from the
# standardized fit) and compute Sam Doe's plug-in (PE), posterior-mean (PM)
# risk, and 95% credible interval from the eta draws.
{
  Xn  <- X[, -1, drop = FALSE]
  ctr <- colMeans(Xn)
  sds <- apply(Xn, 2, sd); sds[sds == 0 | !is.finite(sds)] <- 1
  Xs  <- sweep(sweep(Xn, 2, ctr, "-"), 2, sds, "/")

  fit_brm <- rstan::sampling(
    get_ridge_stanmodel(),
    data    = list(n = nrow(Xs), p = ncol(Xs), X = Xs, y = as.integer(df_sample$Y)),
    chains  = 4, iter = 2000, cores = 1, refresh = 0, seed = settings$seed,
    pars    = c("alpha", "beta", "tau"),
    control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12)
  )
  dr  <- rstan::extract(fit_brm, pars = c("alpha", "beta"))
  a_d <- dr$alpha                                   # D draws of intercept (std scale)
  b_d <- dr$beta                                    # D x p draws of slopes (std scale)

  # Back-transform each draw to the original scale:
  #   beta_orig_j    = beta_std_j / sd_j
  #   intercept_orig = alpha - sum_j beta_std_j * ctr_j / sd_j
  bo_d <- sweep(b_d, 2, sds, "/")
  a0_d <- a_d - as.numeric(b_d %*% (ctr / sds))
  cf_d <- cbind(a0_d, bo_d)                          # D x (p+1): intercept, X1..Xp
  cf_mat <- cbind(estimate = colMeans(cf_d), SE = apply(cf_d, 2, sd))
  rownames(cf_mat) <- colnames(X)                    # (Intercept), X1..X7
  gusto_collector$models$reg_br_mcmc$coefs <- cf_mat

  # Posterior-mean risk for each development-sample individual (for the
  # shrinkage figure): average plogis(eta) over the draws.
  eta_samp <- sweep(Xs %*% t(b_d), 2, a_d, "+")      # n x D
  df_sample$pred_pm_br_mcmc <- rowMeans(plogis(eta_samp))

  # Sam Doe: standardize covariates, form eta draws, summarise.
  xs_doe  <- (settings$Doe[-1] - ctr) / sds
  eta_doe <- a_d + as.numeric(b_d %*% xs_doe)        # D draws of eta for Sam Doe
  gusto_collector$Doe$pred_br_mcmc$pe  <-
    plogis(mean(a0_d) + sum(colMeans(bo_d) * settings$Doe[-1]))   # plug-in at posterior-mean coefs
  gusto_collector$Doe$pred_br_mcmc$pm  <- mean(plogis(eta_doe))    # posterior-mean risk
  gusto_collector$Doe$pred_br_mcmc$cri <-
    plogis(quantile(eta_doe, c(0.025, 0.975), names = FALSE))      # empirical 95% CrI
}


# glmnet adds its own (unpenalised) intercept and standardizes internally, so we
# pass predictors WITHOUT the model-matrix intercept column (matches the
# simulation loop). coef() then returns (Intercept, X1..X7) — no [-2,] needed.
X_noint <- X[, -1, drop = FALSE]

# ---- Frequentist Ridge (cv.glmnet) — no CrI ----
reg_rg <- cv.glmnet(X_noint, df_sample$Y, alpha = 0, family = "binomial", type.measure = "deviance")
gusto_collector$models$reg_rg$coefs <- coef(reg_rg, s = "lambda.min")[, 1]
gusto_collector$models$reg_rg$eq <- coef(reg_rg, s = "lambda.min")
df_sample$pred_ridge_min <- plogis(as.numeric(predict(reg_rg, newx = X_noint, s = "lambda.min")))
gusto_collector$Doe$pred_rg$pe <- plogis(coef(reg_rg, s = "lambda.min")[, 1] %*% settings$Doe)


# ---- Frequentist LASSO (cv.glmnet) ----
# LASSO is no longer shown in the coefficients table (replaced by the MCMC
# ridge), but the fit is retained for the shrinkage visualization (pred_lasso_min).
reg_ls <- cv.glmnet(X_noint, df_sample$Y, alpha = 1, family = "binomial", type.measure = "deviance")
df_sample$pred_lasso_min <- plogis(as.numeric(predict(reg_ls, newx = X_noint, s = "lambda.min")))


model <- reg_j










# ----- Save coefficients table for downstream rendering -----
# Build a wide tidy frame: one row per term, columns alternate est/se
# for models with vcov, est-only for models without. We also persist a
# small metadata vector recording which models have SE so the
# rendering chunk can construct the spanning header without hardcoding.

build_coefs_data <- function(models, digits = 3) {
  # Establish term order from the first model that has named coefs.
  terms <- NULL
  for (m in models) {
    co <- m$coefs
    if (is.null(co)) next
    terms <- if (is.matrix(co) || is.data.frame(co)) rownames(co) else names(co)
    if (!is.null(terms)) break
  }
  if (is.null(terms)) stop("No named coefficients found")

  cols     <- list(Term = terms)
  has_se   <- character(0)  # model keys that have SE
  est_only <- character(0)  # model keys without SE

  for (nm in names(models)) {
    co <- models[[nm]]$coefs
    if (is.null(co)) next
    if ((is.matrix(co) || is.data.frame(co)) && ncol(co) >= 2) {
      cols[[paste0(nm, "_est")]] <- round(co[, 1], digits)
      cols[[paste0(nm, "_se")]]  <- round(co[, 2], digits)
      has_se <- c(has_se, nm)
    } else {
      est_vec <- if (is.matrix(co) || is.data.frame(co)) co[, 1] else as.numeric(co)
      cols[[paste0(nm, "_est")]] <- round(est_vec, digits)
      est_only <- c(est_only, nm)
    }
  }

  list(
    df       = as.data.frame(cols, check.names = FALSE),
    has_se   = has_se,
    est_only = est_only
  )
}

coefs_table_data <- build_coefs_data(gusto_collector$models, digits = 3)

#MS: change X to proper var names
coefs_table_data$df$Term[-1]<-settings$var_specs$short_name[match(coefs_table_data$df$Term[-1], settings$var_specs$key)]

kable(coefs_table_data)

kable(unlist(gusto_collector$Doe))

saveRDS(gusto_collector, file = paste0(res_dir, "gusto_collector.rds"))
saveRDS(coefs_table_data, file = paste0(res_dir, "gusto_coefs_table.rds"))
```

### Visualization

```{r}


lp_pe_f       <- logit(df_sample$pred_pe_f)
lp_pm_f       <- logit(df_sample$pred_pm_f)
lp_ridge      <- logit(df_sample$pred_ridge_min)
lp_pm_br_mcmc <- logit(df_sample$pred_pm_br_mcmc)
lp_pm_j       <- logit(df_sample$pred_pm_j)
lp_pm_lf      <- logit(df_sample$pred_pm_lf)
lp_pm_br      <- logit(df_sample$pred_pm_br)

# Methods are tagged with type (Bayesian PM vs frequentist PE) so the
# plot can colour them differently — the frequentist ridge plug-in is shown in
# grey as a non-Bayesian reference; all posterior means (including the exact
# MCMC ridge) are in the Bayesian-PM colour.
plot_df <- tibble(
  `Posterior Mean - flat`        = lp_pm_f,
  `Posterior Mean - Jeffreys`    = lp_pm_j,
  `Posterior Mean - log-F`       = lp_pm_lf,
  `Posterior Mean - Gaussian`    = lp_pm_br,
  `Plug-in Estimate - Ridge`     = lp_ridge,
  `Posterior Mean - MCMC ridge`  = lp_pm_br_mcmc,
  lp_pe_f                        = lp_pe_f
) %>%
  pivot_longer(-lp_pe_f, names_to = "method", values_to = "lp") %>%
  mutate(
    delta = lp - lp_pe_f,
    method = factor(method, levels = c("Posterior Mean - flat",
                                       "Posterior Mean - Jeffreys",
                                       "Posterior Mean - log-F",
                                       "Posterior Mean - Gaussian",
                                       "Plug-in Estimate - Ridge",
                                       "Posterior Mean - MCMC ridge")),
    method_type = ifelse(grepl("^Posterior Mean", method),
                         "Bayesian PM", "Frequentist PE")
  )



label_df <- data.frame(
  method = unique(plot_df$method),
  label = LETTERS[1:6], 
  x = -Inf, 
  y = Inf
)



plt <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = lp_pe_f, y = delta, color = method_type)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey60", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`Bayesian PM`   = "#2c3e50",
                                `Frequentist PE` = "grey55"),
                     guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ method, nrow = 2) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-1, 2)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.spacing    = unit(1, "lines")
  ) +
  labs(x = expression("Unpenalised linear predictor ("~ eta ~ ")"), y = expression("Δ for each method versus unpenlised " ~ eta))+
  geom_text(data = label_df, 
          aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
          hjust = -7, 
          vjust = 1.5, 
          inherit.aes = FALSE, 
          fontface = "bold", 
          size = 3,
          color = "black")



all_vals <- c(plot_df$lp_pe_f, plot_df$delta)
mx <- max(abs(all_vals), na.rm = TRUE)
lims <- c(-mx, mx)
plt2 <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = lp_pe_f, y = delta, color = method_type)) +

  #coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-0.5, 0.75)) +

  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

    panel.spacing    = unit(1, "lines")
  ) +
  labs(x = expression("Unpenalised linear predictor ("~ eta ~ ")"), y = expression("Δ for each method v. unpeanlised " ~ eta))+
  geom_text(data = label_df, 
          aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
          hjust = -7, 
          vjust = 1.5, 
          inherit.aes = FALSE, 
          fontface = "bold", 
          size = 3,
          color = "black")
```

## Simulation setup
```{r}

sim <- function(i) {
  out <- c()

  # Per-(replicate i, sample-size index j) seeds derived from the master seed
  # settings$seed. Changing it regenerates every replicate's subsample, glmnet
  # folds and MCMC draws; the row is reproducible regardless of worker or run
  # order (required for resuming). Sub-slots: +0 subsample, +1 glmnet folds,
  # +2 ridge MCMC, +3 lasso MCMC, +4 flat MCMC. Keep settings$seed a modest
  # integer so the value stays within R's 32-bit integer seed range.
  sseed <- function(j, s) settings$seed * 1000000L + i * 1000L + j * 100L + s

  for (j in seq_along(settings$ns)) {
    n <- settings$ns[j]
    preds <- NULL

    set.seed(sseed(j, 0L))                 # training subsample for (i, n)
    ids <- sample(nrow(df_final), n)
    df_samp <- df_final[ids, ]
    df_pop  <- df_final[-ids, ]

    mm_samp <- model.matrix(settings$fm_model, df_samp)
    mm_pop  <- model.matrix(settings$fm_model, df_pop)

    set.seed(sseed(j, 1L))                 # modeling RNG (glmnet CV folds)

    # --- Unpenalised MLE family ---
    need_mle <- any(c("pe_f", "pm_f", "pm_f_mk", "pm_f_pp", "pm_f_cpp") %in% settings$methods)
    need_j   <- any(c("pe_j", "pm_j", "pm_j_mk", "pm_j_pp", "pm_j_cpp") %in% settings$methods)
    need_lf  <- any(c("pe_lf", "pm_lf", "pm_lf_mk", "pm_lf_pp", "pm_lf_cpp") %in% settings$methods)
    need_br  <- any(c("pe_br", "pm_br", "pm_br_mk", "pm_br_pp", "pm_br_cpp") %in% settings$methods)

    if (need_mle || need_j) {
      reg <- glm(settings$fm_model, data = df_samp, family = binomial())

      if ("pe_f" %in% settings$methods) {
        preds <- cbind(preds, predict(reg, newdata = df_pop, type = "response"))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pe_f"
      }
      if ("pm_f" %in% settings$methods) {
        preds <- cbind(preds, predict_pm(mm_pop, coef(reg), vcov(reg)))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pm_f"
      }
      if ("pm_f_mk" %in% settings$methods) {
        preds <- cbind(preds, predict_pm(mm_pop, coef(reg), vcov(reg), "mackay"))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pm_f_mk"
      }
      if (any(c("pm_f_pp", "pm_f_cpp") %in% settings$methods)) {
        pm_samp_f <- predict_pm(mm_samp, coef(reg), vcov(reg))
      }
      if ("pm_f_pp" %in% settings$methods) {
        reg_f_pp <- suppressWarnings(glm.fit(mm_samp, pm_samp_f, family = binomial()))
        preds <- cbind(preds, plogis(mm_pop %*% coef(reg_f_pp)))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pm_f_pp"
      }
      if ("pm_f_cpp" %in% settings$methods) {
        cfs <- project_constrained_kl(pm_samp_f, mm_samp, sum(df_samp$Y))
        preds <- cbind(preds, plogis(mm_pop %*% cfs))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pm_f_cpp"
      }
    }

    # --- Firth family ---
    if (need_j) {
      reg_j <- update(reg, method = "brglmFit", type = "AS_mean")

      if ("pe_j" %in% settings$methods) {
        preds <- cbind(preds, predict(reg_j, newdata = df_pop, type = "response"))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pe_j"
      }
      if ("pm_j" %in% settings$methods) {
        preds <- cbind(preds, predict_pm(mm_pop, coef(reg_j), vcov(reg_j)))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pm_j"
      }
      if ("pm_j_mk" %in% settings$methods) {
        preds <- cbind(preds, predict_pm(mm_pop, coef(reg_j), vcov(reg_j), "mackay"))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pm_j_mk"
      }
      if(any(c("pm_j_pp","pm_j_cpp") %in% settings$methods)){
        pm_samp_j  <- predict_pm(mm_samp, coef(reg_j), vcov(reg_j))
      }
      if ("pm_j_pp" %in% settings$methods) {
        reg_j_pp <- suppressWarnings(glm.fit(mm_samp, pm_samp_j, family = binomial()))
        preds <- cbind(preds, plogis(mm_pop %*% coef(reg_j_pp)))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pm_j_pp"
      }
      if ("pm_j_cpp" %in% settings$methods) {
        cfs <- project_constrained_kl(pm_samp_j, mm_samp, sum(df_samp$Y))
        preds <- cbind(preds, plogis(mm_pop %*% cfs))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pm_j_cpp"
      }
    }

    # --- log-F(m, m) family ---
    # Weakly-informative shrinkage prior on slopes; intercept flat.
    # See Greenland & Mansournia 2015. logf_glm() is in core.R.
    if (need_lf) {
      reg_lf <- logf_glm(mm_samp, df_samp$Y, m = settings$logf_m)

      if ("pe_lf" %in% settings$methods) {
        preds <- cbind(preds, plogis(mm_pop %*% coef(reg_lf)))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pe_lf"
      }
      if ("pm_lf" %in% settings$methods) {
        preds <- cbind(preds, predict_pm(mm_pop, coef(reg_lf), vcov(reg_lf)))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pm_lf"
      }
      if ("pm_lf_mk" %in% settings$methods) {
        preds <- cbind(preds, predict_pm(mm_pop, coef(reg_lf), vcov(reg_lf), "mackay"))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pm_lf_mk"
      }
      if (any(c("pm_lf_pp", "pm_lf_cpp") %in% settings$methods)) {
        pm_samp_lf <- predict_pm(mm_samp, coef(reg_lf), vcov(reg_lf))
      }
      if ("pm_lf_pp" %in% settings$methods) {
        reg_lf_pp <- suppressWarnings(glm.fit(mm_samp, pm_samp_lf, family = binomial()))
        preds <- cbind(preds, plogis(mm_pop %*% coef(reg_lf_pp)))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pm_lf_pp"
      }
      if ("pm_lf_cpp" %in% settings$methods) {
        cfs <- project_constrained_kl(pm_samp_lf, mm_samp, sum(df_samp$Y))
        preds <- cbind(preds, plogis(mm_pop %*% cfs))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pm_lf_cpp"
      }
    }
    
    # --- Bayesian ridge family ---
    if (need_br) {
      reg_br <- bayesian_ridge(mm_samp, df_samp$Y)

      if ("pe_br" %in% settings$methods) {
        preds <- cbind(preds, plogis(mm_pop %*% reg_br$beta))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pe_br"
      }
      if ("pm_br" %in% settings$methods) {
        preds <- cbind(preds, predict_pm(mm_pop, reg_br$beta, reg_br$V))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pm_br"
      }
      if ("pm_br_mk" %in% settings$methods) {
        preds <- cbind(preds, predict_pm(mm_pop, reg_br$beta, reg_br$V, "mackay"))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pm_br_mk"
      }
      if (any(c("pm_br_pp", "pm_br_cpp") %in% settings$methods)) {
        pm_samp_br <- predict_pm(mm_samp, reg_br$beta, reg_br$V)
      }
      if ("pm_br_pp" %in% settings$methods) {
        reg_br_pp <- suppressWarnings(glm.fit(mm_samp, pm_samp_br, family = binomial()))
        preds <- cbind(preds, plogis(mm_pop %*% coef(reg_br_pp)))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pm_br_pp"
      }
      if ("pm_br_cpp" %in% settings$methods) {
        cfs <- project_constrained_kl(pm_samp_br, mm_samp, sum(df_samp$Y))
        preds <- cbind(preds, plogis(mm_pop %*% cfs))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pm_br_cpp"
      }
    }

    # --- MCMC Bayesian Ridge (static Stan) and Bayesian LASSO (rstanarm) ---
    # Ridge: fit_ridge_stan() (core.R) fits a hand-written Stan model whose
    # common shrinkage scale tau is ESTIMATED via a half-Student-t hyperprior
    # — the faithful Bayesian analogue of mgcv's REML ridge. Predictors are
    # standardized to training SD = 1 so a single shared tau penalizes all
    # slopes equally (= mgcv's S = I); the intercept has no prior (flat). The
    # Stan model is compiled once per worker and reused via rstan::sampling;
    # the PM is computed from the draws in row-chunks to bound peak RAM.
    #
    # LASSO: rstanarm::stan_glm(prior = lasso()) — the standard Park & Casella
    # Bayesian lasso, precompiled. Its global penalty is given a hyperprior and
    # ESTIMATED from the data (data-adaptive shrinkage, analogous to CV-tuned
    # glmnet), so it is hierarchical despite the fixed prior-family call.
    # prior_intercept = NULL leaves the intercept flat, matching glmnet.
    #
    # Both: cores = 1 (parallelism comes from the foreach chunk loop).
    # Convergence is diagnosed but does NOT gate inclusion: MCMC is always
    # evaluated on the same replicates as every other method. Excluding
    # non-converged replicates would give MCMC a cherry-picked evaluation set
    # (only easy replicates) and inflate its apparent performance. Diagnostics
    # are returned as an attribute for reporting.
    need_br_mcmc    <- "pm_br_mcmc"    %in% settings$methods
    need_lasso_mcmc <- "pm_lasso_mcmc" %in% settings$methods
    need_f_mcmc     <- "pm_f_mcmc"     %in% settings$methods
    mcmc_diag <- list()

    if (need_br_mcmc) {
      res_mcmc <- fit_ridge_stan(mm_samp[, -1, drop = FALSE], df_samp$Y,
                                 mm_pop[, -1, drop = FALSE],
                                 seed = sseed(j, 2L))
      if (!is.null(res_mcmc)) {
        mcmc_diag$pm_br_mcmc <- res_mcmc[c("rhat_max", "n_diverg", "converged")]
        preds <- cbind(preds, res_mcmc$pm)
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pm_br_mcmc"
      }
    }

    if (need_lasso_mcmc) {
      fit_lasso_mcmc <- tryCatch(
        rstanarm::stan_glm(
          settings$fm_model, data = df_samp, family = binomial(),
          prior            = rstanarm::lasso(autoscale = TRUE),
          prior_intercept  = NULL,   # flat intercept — matches glmnet
          cores = 1, chains = 4, iter = 2000, refresh = 0,
          seed = sseed(j, 3L)
        ),
        error = function(e) NULL
      )
      if (!is.null(fit_lasso_mcmc)) {
        rhat_max <- max(fit_lasso_mcmc$stan_summary[, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE)
        n_diverg <- sum(sapply(
          rstan::get_sampler_params(fit_lasso_mcmc$stanfit, inc_warmup = FALSE),
          function(sp) sum(sp[, "divergent__"])
        ))
        mcmc_diag$pm_lasso_mcmc <- list(rhat_max = rhat_max, n_diverg = n_diverg,
                                        converged = n_diverg == 0 && rhat_max < 1.01)
        pm_vec <- colMeans(rstanarm::posterior_epred(fit_lasso_mcmc, newdata = df_pop))
        preds  <- cbind(preds, pm_vec)
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pm_lasso_mcmc"
      }
    }

    # Flat-prior MCMC: rstanarm::stan_glm(prior = NULL, prior_intercept = NULL)
    # gives flat (improper uniform) priors on all coefficients AND the
    # intercept, so the posterior is proportional to the likelihood. Its
    # posterior-mean risk is the EXACT flat-prior PM that pm_f approximates via
    # Laplace (MLE mode + Hessian-based vcov). Comparing pm_f_mcmc vs pm_f
    # therefore isolates the pure effect of the Laplace approximation, with no
    # prior differences confounding it.
    if (need_f_mcmc) {
      fit_f_mcmc <- tryCatch(
        rstanarm::stan_glm(
          settings$fm_model, data = df_samp, family = binomial(),
          prior            = NULL,   # flat (improper) prior on slopes
          prior_intercept  = NULL,   # flat (improper) prior on intercept
          cores = 1, chains = 4, iter = 2000, refresh = 0,
          seed = sseed(j, 4L)
        ),
        error = function(e) NULL
      )
      if (!is.null(fit_f_mcmc)) {
        rhat_max <- max(fit_f_mcmc$stan_summary[, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE)
        n_diverg <- sum(sapply(
          rstan::get_sampler_params(fit_f_mcmc$stanfit, inc_warmup = FALSE),
          function(sp) sum(sp[, "divergent__"])
        ))
        mcmc_diag$pm_f_mcmc <- list(rhat_max = rhat_max, n_diverg = n_diverg,
                                    converged = n_diverg == 0 && rhat_max < 1.01)
        pm_vec <- colMeans(rstanarm::posterior_epred(fit_f_mcmc, newdata = df_pop))
        preds  <- cbind(preds, pm_vec)
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pm_f_mcmc"
      }
    }

    # glmnet adds its own (unpenalised) intercept and standardizes internally,
    # so we pass the predictors WITHOUT the model-matrix intercept column —
    # mirroring the synthetic sim and avoiding feeding glmnet a constant column.
    mm_samp_noint <- mm_samp[, -1, drop = FALSE]
    mm_pop_noint  <- mm_pop[, -1, drop = FALSE]

    # --- LASSO ---
    if (any(c("pe_lasso_min", "pe_lasso_1se") %in% settings$methods)) {
      reg_s <- cv.glmnet(mm_samp_noint, df_samp$Y, family = "binomial",
                         type.measure = "deviance")
      if ("pe_lasso_min" %in% settings$methods) {
        preds <- cbind(preds, as.numeric(
          predict(reg_s, newx = mm_pop_noint, s = "lambda.min", type = "response")
        ))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pe_lasso_min"
      }
      if ("pe_lasso_1se" %in% settings$methods) {
        preds <- cbind(preds, as.numeric(
          predict(reg_s, newx = mm_pop_noint, s = "lambda.1se", type = "response")
        ))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pe_lasso_1se"
      }
    }

    # --- Ridge ---
    if (any(c("pe_ridge_min", "pe_ridge_1se") %in% settings$methods)) {
      reg_s <- cv.glmnet(mm_samp_noint, df_samp$Y, alpha = 0, family = "binomial",
                         type.measure = "deviance")
      if ("pe_ridge_min" %in% settings$methods) {
        preds <- cbind(preds, as.numeric(
          predict(reg_s, newx = mm_pop_noint, s = "lambda.min", type = "response")
        ))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pe_ridge_min"
      }
      if ("pe_ridge_1se" %in% settings$methods) {
        preds <- cbind(preds, as.numeric(
          predict(reg_s, newx = mm_pop_noint, s = "lambda.1se", type = "response")
        ))
        colnames(preds)[ncol(preds)] <- "pe_ridge_1se"
      }
    }

    # --- Metrics ---
    iter_res <- list()
    method_names <- colnames(preds)

    if ("mse" %in% settings$metrics) {
      values <- colMeans((preds - df_pop$Y)^2)
      iter_res$mse <- data.frame(metric = "mse", method = method_names, value = values)
    }

    if ("cstat" %in% settings$metrics) {
      values <- sapply(seq_len(ncol(preds)), function(j) {
        as.numeric(pROC::auc(df_pop$Y, preds[, j], quiet = TRUE))
      })
      iter_res$cstat <- data.frame(metric = "cstat", method = method_names, value = values)
    }

    if ("oe_ratio" %in% settings$metrics) {
      obs <- sum(df_pop$Y)
      values <- obs / colSums(preds)
      iter_res$oe_ratio <- data.frame(metric = "oe_ratio", method = method_names, value = values)
    }

    if ("cal_slp" %in% settings$metrics) {
      values <- sapply(seq_len(ncol(preds)), function(j) {
        p_adj   <- pmin(pmax(preds[, j], 1e-15), 1 - 1e-15)
        logit_p <- log(p_adj / (1 - p_adj))
        fit_cal <- suppressWarnings(
          glm.fit(cbind(1, logit_p), df_pop$Y, family = binomial())
        )
        slp <- fit_cal$coefficients[2]
        # Degenerate predictions (LASSO/ridge shrunk to near-constant) → null model
        if (!isTRUE(fit_cal$converged) || is.na(slp)) slp <- 0
        unname(slp)
      })
      iter_res$cal_slp <- data.frame(metric = "cal_slp", method = method_names, value = values)
    }

    if ("nb" %in% settings$metrics) {
      scen_prev <- mean(df_pop$Y)
      iter_res$nb <- data.frame()
      for (z in settings$z) {
        nb_term <- df_pop$Y - (1 - df_pop$Y) * z / (1 - z)
        nb0 <- max(0, mean(nb_term))
        values <- sapply(seq_len(ncol(preds)), function(j) {
          mean((preds[, j] > z) * nb_term - nb0)/scen_prev   # standardized NB (divided by prevalence)
        })
        iter_res$nb <- rbind(
          iter_res$nb,
          data.frame(metric = paste0("nb", z), method = method_names, value = values)
        )
      }
    }

    iter_df <- cbind(n = n, do.call(rbind, iter_res))
    if (length(mcmc_diag) > 0) {
      attr(iter_df, "mcmc_diag") <- mcmc_diag
    }
    out <- rbind(out, iter_df)
  }

  cbind(iteration = i, out)
}

```


## Simulations
```{r}
n_sim <- settings$n_sim

# =========================================================================
# Resumable checkpointing (mirrors the synthetic sim).
#
# The unit of work is a replicate i in 1..n_sim (each does all sample sizes).
# Every replicate is fully self-seeded (see sim()), so its result is identical
# regardless of worker / run order — which is what makes resuming safe.
#
# Run signature = science-relevant settings + master seed. Match -> RESUME
# (keep completed replicate files, run only the missing ones). Mismatch / none
# -> FRESH (wipe dump_dir). Execution-only choices (cores) are excluded.
# =========================================================================
rows_dir <- file.path(dump_dir, "reps")
sig_file <- file.path(dump_dir, "run_signature.rds")

run_signature <- list(
  methods  = settings$methods, metrics = settings$metrics, ns = settings$ns,
  n_sim    = settings$n_sim,    logf_m  = settings$logf_m, z  = settings$z,
  fm_model = paste(deparse(settings$fm_model), collapse = " "),
  seed     = settings$seed
)
resume <- file.exists(sig_file) && identical(readRDS(sig_file), run_signature)

if (resume) {
  message("Run signature matches ", dump_dir, " -> RESUMING.")
} else {
  message("New/changed run signature -> starting FRESH (clearing ", dump_dir, ").")
  if (dir.exists(dump_dir)) unlink(dump_dir, recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE)
  dir.create(rows_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(run_signature, sig_file)
  saveRDS(settings, file.path(dump_dir, "settings.rds"))
}
dir.create(rows_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Pending = replicates without a completed file, in randomized dispatch order
# (homogeneous progress + order-independent load). Seeded for a reproducible
# dispatch order; results are per-replicate deterministic regardless.
done_files <- list.files(rows_dir, pattern = "^rep_[0-9]+\\.rds$")
done_idx   <- as.integer(sub("^rep_0*([0-9]+)\\.rds$", "\\1", done_files))
pending    <- setdiff(seq_len(n_sim), done_idx)
set.seed(settings$seed)
pending <- pending[sample(length(pending))]
message(sprintf("Replicates: %d total, %d done, %d pending.",
                n_sim, n_sim - length(pending), length(pending)))

# Exactly ONE line is written per replicate processed, so the log line count is
# a direct progress measure. Run-start / chunk markers go to the console only.
progress_file <- file.path(dump_dir, "sim_gusto_progress.log")
message(sprintf("=== run start: %d pending of %d ===", length(pending), n_sim))
message("Worker progress log: ", progress_file)

if (length(pending) > 0) {
  chunks     <- split(pending, ceiling(seq_along(pending) / chunk_size))
  n_chunks   <- length(chunks)

  no_cores <- if (is.null(n_cores)) {
    min(parallel::detectCores() - 1, n_chunks)
  } else n_cores

  if (no_cores > 1) {
    cl <- makeCluster(no_cores)
    registerDoSNOW(cl)
    parallel::clusterExport(cl, varlist = c(
      "df_final", "settings", "sim", "chunks", "n_chunks",
      "progress_file", "rows_dir"
    ))
    clusterCall(cl, function() source("core.R"))
    message(paste("Running in PARALLEL on", no_cores, "cores,", n_chunks, "chunks"))
  } else {
    registerDoSEQ(); cl <- NULL
    message("Running SEQUENTIALLY")
  }

  # Per-replicate atomic writes make this resumable; workers return only the
  # completed indices (results live on disk), keeping master memory flat.
  done_now <- foreach(
    ch = seq_len(n_chunks),
    .combine = c,
    .packages = c("glmnet", "mvtnorm", "pROC", "brglm2", "rstan", "rstanarm"),
    .errorhandling = "pass"
  ) %dopar% {
    reps <- chunks[[ch]]
    completed <- integer(0)
    for (i in reps) {
      # One line per replicate processed (line count == progress).
      log_progress(sprintf("replicate %d", i), progress_file)
      out_i <- tryCatch(
        sim(i),
        error = function(e) {
          log_progress(sprintf("replicate %d ERROR: %s", i, conditionMessage(e)),
                       progress_file)
          data.frame(iteration = i, n = NA, metric = NA, method = NA, value = NA,
                     error_msg = conditionMessage(e), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
        }
      )
      save_row_atomic(out_i, file.path(rows_dir, sprintf("rep_%06d.rds", i)))
      completed <- c(completed, i)
    }
    completed
  }

  if (!is.null(cl)) stopCluster(cl)
  message(sprintf("Completed %d replicates this run.", length(unlist(done_now))))
} else {
  message("Nothing pending; all replicates already complete.")
}

# --- Combine all completed replicate files ---
all_files <- list.files(rows_dir, pattern = "^rep_[0-9]+\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
res <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(all_files, readRDS))
message(sprintf("Combined %d replicate files -> %d result rows.",
                length(all_files), nrow(res)))

# Separate any captured errors (NA metric / error_msg) from the results.
if ("error_msg" %in% names(res)) {
  err <- res[!is.na(res$error_msg), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(err) > 0) {
    message(sprintf("%d replicate(s) errored; saved to %s.",
                    length(unique(err$iteration)), file.path(dump_dir, "sim_gusto_errors.rds")))
    saveRDS(err, file.path(dump_dir, "sim_gusto_errors.rds"))
  }
  res <- res[is.na(res$error_msg), , drop = FALSE]
  res$error_msg <- NULL
}

res$metric <- as.factor(res$metric)
res$method <- as.factor(res$method)

# Report NA / outlier rate in cal_slp for sanity
if ("cal_slp" %in% settings$metrics) {
  cal_summary <- res %>%
    filter(as.character(metric) == "cal_slp") %>%
    group_by(method) %>%
    summarise(
      n        = n(),
      n_zero   = sum(value == 0),
      n_extreme = sum(!is.na(value) & abs(value) > 3),
      .groups  = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(n_zero > 0 | n_extreme > 0)
  if (nrow(cal_summary) > 0) {
    cat("\nDegenerate / extreme cal_slp (replaced NA with 0):\n")
    print(as.data.frame(cal_summary), row.names = FALSE)
  }
}

# MCMC hard-failure rate (fit crashed entirely — tryCatch returned NULL)
# Uses n_distinct(iteration) so row-count differences across metrics never mislead.
mcmc_methods <- c("pm_br_mcmc", "pm_lasso_mcmc", "pm_f_mcmc")

n_iter_per_n <- res %>%
  group_by(n) %>%
  summarise(n_expected = n_distinct(iteration), .groups = "drop")

mcmc_conv <- res %>%
  filter(as.character(method) %in% mcmc_methods) %>%
  group_by(method, n) %>%
  summarise(n_present = n_distinct(iteration), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(n_iter_per_n, by = "n") %>%
  mutate(n_failed   = n_expected - n_present,
         pct_failed = round(100 * n_failed / n_expected, 1))

# Also add rows for MCMC methods with zero presence (crashed every replicate)
for (m in mcmc_methods) {
  missing_ns <- setdiff(n_iter_per_n$n, mcmc_conv$n[mcmc_conv$method == m])
  if (length(missing_ns) > 0) {
    mcmc_conv <- bind_rows(mcmc_conv,
      n_iter_per_n %>% filter(n %in% missing_ns) %>%
        mutate(method = m, n_present = 0L,
               n_failed = n_expected, pct_failed = 100))
  }
}

if (any(mcmc_conv$n_failed > 0)) {
  cat("\nMCMC hard failures (fit crashed — excluded from results):\n")
  print(as.data.frame(mcmc_conv[mcmc_conv$n_failed > 0, ]), row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("\nMCMC: no hard failures (all replicates returned predictions).\n")
}

saveRDS(res, file = file.path(res_dir, "sim_gusto_results.rds"))
```

```{r}

res <- readRDS(file.path(res_dir, "sim_gusto_results.RDS"))

# Switch: if TRUE, the main plot is anchored to the plug-in flat-prior method
# (pe_f) as reference — values shifted to pe_f's own mean/median, whiskers are
# the paired difference vs pe_f. Set FALSE for the plain absolute plot.
rel_to_pe_f <- FALSE

# Switch: if TRUE, the PM-computation figure is anchored to Gauss-Hermite
# quadrature ("exact") as the reference — each computation method is shown as a
# paired difference vs exact, positioned at exact's own mean/median value.
comp_rel_to_exact <- FALSE

default_metric_order <- c("mse", "cstat", "oe_ratio", "cal_slp"
                          #,"nb0.02", "nb0.05", "nb0.1"
                          )



# =========================================================================
# Main-effects plots, styled to match the synthetic-simulation figures:
#   rows = metrics, x = n, point + whiskers, methods dodged
#   centrality: mean for most metrics; median for cal_slp and oe_ratio
#   (heavy-tailed). Whiskers always show the IQR (Q25, Q75) across
#   replicates — chosen so they stay within metric ranges (e.g., MSE
#   non-negative) and are robust to outlier replicates.
# =========================================================================

# =========================================================================
# Method registry — single source of truth for plotting.
#
# Each method gets one row. The four lookup vectors used by the plot
# builders (method_labels, method_colors, method_shapes, and the default
# display order) are derived from this. To add a new method to the plots,
# add a single row and nothing else.
#
# Naming convention (just documentation; not enforced by the code):
#   <estimator>_<prior>[_<computation>]
#     estimator : pe (point estimate) or pm (posterior mean)
#     prior     : f (flat), j (Jeffreys), lf (log-F), ridge, lasso, br, ...
#     comp.     : omitted = quadrature (exact); mk = MacKay;
#                 pp = self-projection; cpp = constrained self-proj.;
#                 min, 1se for CV-based LASSO/ridge
# =========================================================================

q_range <- c(0.25, 0.75)

method_registry <- tibble::tribble(
  ~key,            ~label,                                 ~color,     ~shape,
  "pe_f",          "PE (flat)",                           "#1F4E79",  1,
  "pm_f",          "PM (flat)",                           "#1F4E79",  16,
  "pm_f_mk",       "PM (flat, MacKay)",                   "#1F4E79",  16,
  "pm_f_pp",       "PM (flat, self-proj.)",               "#1F4E79",  16,
  "pm_f_cpp",      "PM (flat, constr. self-proj.)",       "#1F4E79",  16,

  "pe_j",          "PE (Jeffreys)",                       "#884553",  0,
  "pm_j",          "PM (Jeffreys)",                       "#884553",  15,
  "pm_j_mk",       "PM (Jeffreys, MacKay)",               "#884553",  15,
  "pm_j_pp",       "PM (Jeffreys, self-proj.)",           "#884553",  15,
  "pm_j_cpp",      "PM (Jeffreys, constr. self-proj.)",   "#884553",  15,

  "pe_lf",         "PE (log-F)",                          "#009E73",  2,
  "pm_lf",         "PM (logF)",                           "#009E73",  17,
  "pm_lf_mk",      "PM (logF, MacKay)",                   "#009E73",  17,
  "pm_lf_pp",      "PM (logF, self-proj.)",               "#009E73",  17,
  "pm_lf_cpp",     "PM (logF, constr. self-proj.)",       "#009E73",  17,

  "pe_br",         "PE (Bayes. ridge)",                       "#E07B00",  5,
  "pm_br",         "PM (Bayes. ridge)",                       "#E07B00",  18,
  "pm_br_mk",      "PM (Bayes. ridge, MacKay)",               "#E07B00",  18,
  "pm_br_pp",      "PM (Bayes. ridge, self-proj.)",           "#E07B00",  18,
  "pm_br_cpp",     "PM (Bayes. ridge, constr. self-proj.)",   "#E07B00",  18,

  "pe_ridge_min",  "PE (Ridge)",                       "#AAAAAA",  2,
  "pe_lasso_min",  "PE (LASSO)",                       "#AAAAAA",  6,

  "pm_br_mcmc",    "PM (MCMC ridge)",                      "#666666",  8,
  "pm_lasso_mcmc", "PM (MCMC LASSO)",                      "#666666",  8,
  "pm_f_mcmc",     "PM (MCMC flat)",                       "#666666",  7,
)


# ---- Derive lookup vectors ----
method_labels <- setNames(method_registry$label, method_registry$key)
method_colors <- setNames(method_registry$color, method_registry$key)
method_shapes <- setNames(method_registry$shape, method_registry$key)
default_method_order <- method_registry$key

metric_labels <- c(
  mse      = "MSE",
  cstat    = "C-statistic",
  oe_ratio = "O/E ratio",
  cal_slp  = "Calibration slope",
  nb0.02   = "sNB (z = 0.02)",
  nb0.05   = "sNB (z = 0.05)",
  nb0.1    = "sNB (z = 0.10)"
)



metric_reference <- list(
  cal_slp  = 1,
  oe_ratio = 1
)

# ---- Per-metric summary specification ----
# For each metric, independently choose:
#   - `center`: which centrality to display ("mean" or "median")
#   - `range` : how to compute lower/upper whiskers ("sd" or "quant")
# When range = "quant", the quantile pair comes from the global q_range
# vector (default: c(0.25, 0.75)).
# To override for a particular plot, pass a modified list to the
# `summary_spec` argument of build_plot()/build_computation_plot().
# Whisker type for the mean-based metrics: "se" (mean +/- SE = sd/sqrt(n)) or
# "sd" (mean +/- SD). Flip this one value and RE-RUN this whole chunk (it must
# be re-evaluated before build_plot() is called). oe_ratio / cal_slp stay on
# median + IQR ("quant") because they are heavy-tailed.
whisker_type <- "sd"

metric_summary_spec <- list(
  mse      = list(center = "mean",   range = whisker_type),
  cstat    = list(center = "mean",   range = whisker_type),
  oe_ratio = list(center = "median", range = "quant"),
  cal_slp  = list(center = "median", range = "quant"),
  nb0.02   = list(center = "mean",   range = whisker_type),
  nb0.05   = list(center = "mean",   range = whisker_type),
  nb0.1    = list(center = "mean",   range = whisker_type)
)

# ---- Centrality / whisker helpers ----
# Each helper takes the per-metric data vector x and a single-string
# spec, returning a scalar. compute_lower / compute_upper are split
# (rather than one helper returning length-2) so that summarise() can
# call them directly without list-unpacking.

compute_center <- function(x, spec) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x) < 1) return(NA_real_)
  switch(spec,
         mean   = mean(x),
         median = median(x),
         stop("Unknown centrality spec: ", spec))
}

compute_lower <- function(x, spec) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  switch(spec,
         se = mean(x) - sd(x)/sqrt(length(x)),
         sd    = mean(x) - sd(x),
         quant = unname(quantile(x, q_range[1], na.rm = TRUE)),
         stop("Unknown range spec: ", spec))
}

compute_upper <- function(x, spec) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  switch(spec,
         se = mean(x) + sd(x)/sqrt(length(x)),
         sd    = mean(x) + sd(x),
         quant = unname(quantile(x, q_range[2], na.rm = TRUE)),
         stop("Unknown range spec: ", spec))
}

# Resolve the metric's summary spec at aggregation time. `metric_key`
# is the lowercase key (e.g., "mse"), not the display label. Returns
# the list (center, range) for that metric, falling back to mean+quant
# if the metric isn't in the spec.
get_summary_spec <- function(metric_key, spec_table = metric_summary_spec) {
  s <- spec_table[[metric_key]]
  if (is.null(s)) return(list(center = "mean", range = "quant"))
  s
}

# Prepare data: relabel metric values, keep method as character
res_plot <- res %>%
  mutate(
    method = as.character(method),
    metric = as.character(metric)
  ) %>%
  mutate(metric = ifelse(metric %in% names(metric_labels),
                         metric_labels[metric], metric))


build_plot <- function(data, figure_title = NULL,
                       method_order  = default_method_order,
                       metric_order  = default_metric_order,
                       summary_spec  = metric_summary_spec,
                       ref_method    = NULL) {

  # Optional reference mode: express every metric as a PAIRED difference from
  # `ref_method` (e.g. "pe_f" = plug-in flat prior). For each replicate, n and
  # metric we subtract that replicate's own ref value, so the reference method
  # sits exactly at 0 and the whiskers reflect within-replicate variation of the
  # difference (much tighter and more interpretable than differencing means).
  rel_mode <- !is.null(ref_method)
  if (rel_mode) {
    if (!any(as.character(data$method) == ref_method)) {
      warning("ref_method '", ref_method, "' not in data; plotting absolute values.")
      rel_mode <- FALSE
    } else {
      ref_vals <- data %>%
        filter(as.character(method) == ref_method) %>%
        select(iteration, n, metric, .ref_value = value)
      data <- data %>%
        inner_join(ref_vals, by = c("iteration", "n", "metric")) %>%
        mutate(value = value - .ref_value) %>%
        select(-.ref_value)
    }
  }

  # Method ordering. Keep only methods that (a) appear in the data AND
  # (b) are known to method_labels/colors/shapes AND (c) are either point
  # estimates or quadrature PMs. Non-quadrature PM variants (_mk / _pp /
  # _cpp) are automatically excluded from the main plot — they belong on
  # the dedicated computation-comparison plot. This isolates the prior
  # comparison from the deployment-method comparison.
  comp_suffixes <- c("mk", "pp", "cpp")  # Laplace approximation variants — excluded from main plot
  is_main_plot_method <- function(k) {
    parts <- strsplit(k, "_", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    if (length(parts) < 1) return(FALSE)
    if (parts[1] == "pe") return(TRUE)
    if (parts[1] == "pm") {
      if (length(parts) <= 2) return(TRUE)
      return(!parts[length(parts)] %in% comp_suffixes)  # allow e.g. pm_br_mcmc
    }
    TRUE  # any other prefix (e.g. user-added) passes through
  }
  avail <- unique(as.character(data$method))
  known <- names(method_labels)
  candidates <- intersect(avail, known)
  candidates <- candidates[vapply(candidates, is_main_plot_method, logical(1))]
  method_order <- method_order[method_order %in% candidates]
  extra <- setdiff(candidates, method_order)
  method_order <- c(method_order, extra)

  data <- data %>%
    filter(as.character(method) %in% method_order) %>%
    mutate(method = factor(method, levels = method_order))

  data <- data %>%
    filter(as.character(metric) %in% metric_labels[metric_order]) %>%
    mutate(metric = factor(as.character(metric),
                           levels = metric_labels[metric_order]))

  # Per-metric aggregation. The summary spec for each metric (centrality
  # and range type) is looked up via metric_summary_spec; see helpers
  # compute_center / compute_lower / compute_upper.
  data$metric_key <- names(metric_labels)[match(as.character(data$metric),
                                                metric_labels)]

  agg <- data %>%
    group_by(metric, metric_key, method, n) %>%
    summarise(
      n_sim  = sum(!is.na(value)),
      center = compute_center(value, get_summary_spec(first(metric_key), summary_spec)$center),
      lo     = compute_lower(value, get_summary_spec(first(metric_key), summary_spec)$range),
      hi     = compute_upper(value, get_summary_spec(first(metric_key), summary_spec)$range),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    select(metric, method, n, center, lo, hi)

  # In reference mode the values are paired differences (ref_method at 0). Shift
  # every panel UP by the reference method's own centre (its mean/median on the
  # original scale), so the reference sits at its true value rather than 0 and
  # the whole panel reads on the metric's natural scale — while the whiskers
  # remain the tight paired-difference whiskers.
  if (rel_mode) {
    ref_center_df <- ref_vals %>%
      mutate(mkey       = names(metric_labels)[match(as.character(metric), metric_labels)],
             metric_chr = as.character(metric)) %>%
      group_by(metric_chr, n) %>%
      summarise(ref_center = compute_center(
                  .ref_value, get_summary_spec(first(mkey), summary_spec)$center),
                .groups = "drop")
    agg <- agg %>%
      mutate(metric_chr = as.character(metric)) %>%
      left_join(ref_center_df, by = c("metric_chr", "n")) %>%
      mutate(center = center + ref_center,
             lo     = lo + ref_center,
             hi     = hi + ref_center) %>%
      select(-metric_chr, -ref_center)
  }

  # Guide lines: the metrics' natural targets (cal_slp = 1, oe_ratio = 1) in BOTH
  # modes. After the shift above, the reference-mode axis is on the metric's own
  # scale, so y = 1 is the correct calibration target (not 0, not the ref value).
  ref_df <- data.frame(
    metric_key = names(metric_reference),
    yint       = unlist(metric_reference)
  ) %>%
    mutate(metric = factor(metric_labels[metric_key],
                           levels = metric_labels[metric_order])) %>%
    filter(!is.na(metric)) %>%
    select(metric, yint)

  dodge_width <- 0.6

  p <- ggplot(agg, aes(x = factor(n), y = center,
                       color = method, shape = method, group = method)) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
                  width = 0.3,
                  position = position_dodge(width = dodge_width),
                  linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_point(size = 2,
               position = position_dodge(width = dodge_width)) +
    ggh4x::facet_grid2(
      rows = vars(metric),
      scales = "free_y",
      independent = "y"
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = method_colors, labels = method_labels[method_order],
                       breaks = method_order, drop = FALSE, name = "Method") +
    scale_shape_manual(values = method_shapes, labels = method_labels[method_order],
                       breaks = method_order, drop = FALSE, name = "Method") +
    labs(
      title    = NULL,
      subtitle = if (rel_mode)
        paste0("Whiskers = paired difference vs ", method_labels[ref_method],
               " (positioned on the metric's own scale)") else NULL,
      x = "Training sample size",
      y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      legend.position    = "bottom",
      legend.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
      strip.background   = element_rect(fill = "grey92", colour = NA),
      strip.text         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
      strip.text.y       = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle      = element_text(colour = "grey35", size = 9),
      axis.text.x        = element_text(size = 9)
    ) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
           shape = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))

  if (nrow(ref_df) > 0) {
    p <- p + geom_hline(
      data = ref_df,
      aes(yintercept = yint),
      linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4,
      inherit.aes = FALSE
    )
  }

  list(plot=p, data=agg)
}

fig <- build_plot(res_plot, NULL,
                  ref_method = if (rel_to_pe_f) "pe_f" else NULL)
print(fig$plot)

# Save (separate filename in reference mode so it doesn't overwrite the absolute plot)
main_png <- "sim_gusto_main.png"
ggsave(paste0(res_dir, main_png), fig$plot, width = 9, height = 14, dpi = 200)


# =========================================================================
# PM computation-method comparison plot
#
# Holds the prior fixed within each column (Flat / Jeffreys / log-F /
# Bayesian ridge) and varies the PM computation method (quadrature /
# MacKay / self-projection / CITL-preserving self-projection) within each
# panel. Y-axis matches the main plot per metric, so the reader can see
# directly that computation choice has much smaller effect than prior
# choice.
# =========================================================================

computation_labels <- c(
  exact = "Quadrature (exact)",
  mk    = "MacKay",
  pp    = "Self-proj." #,cpp   = "CITL-preserving seld-proj."
)
computation_colors <- c(
  exact = "#1F4E79",
  mk    = "#2E75B6",
  pp    = "#E07B00" #,cpp   = "#B22222"
)
computation_shapes <- c(
  exact = 16,
  mk    = 17,
  pp    = 15,
  cpp   = 18
)
computation_order <- c("exact", "mk", "pp") #, "cpp")

family_labels <- c(
  f  = "Flat prior",
  j  = "Jeffreys (Firth)",
  lf = "log-F(2, 2)",
  br = "Bayesian ridge"
)
family_order <- c("f", "j", "lf", "br")

parse_pm_method <- function(key) {
  parts <- strsplit(key, "_", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  if (length(parts) < 2 || parts[1] != "pm") {
    return(c(family = NA_character_, computation = NA_character_))
  }
  fam  <- parts[2]
  comp <- if (length(parts) == 2) "exact" else parts[3]
  c(family = fam, computation = comp)
}




# ---- Capture per-metric y-limits from the main plot's aggregation ----
# Replicates the central+whisker computation but extracts only the
# per-metric (ymin, ymax) range across all methods, so the computation
# plot can match exactly.
get_main_plot_ylims <- function(data,
                                method_order  = default_method_order,
                                metric_order  = default_metric_order,
                                summary_spec  = metric_summary_spec) {
  # Apply the same method filter that build_plot uses: keep only PE and
  # quadrature-PM methods. This is essential — if the comp plot inherits
  # y-limits computed across all PM variants, its rows become wider than
  # the corresponding rows of the main plot, and the visual comparison
  # "loss in PM accuracy vs difference between priors" is distorted.
  comp_suffixes <- c("mk", "pp", "cpp")
  is_main_plot_method <- function(k) {
    parts <- strsplit(k, "_", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    if (length(parts) < 1) return(FALSE)
    if (parts[1] == "pe") return(TRUE)
    if (parts[1] == "pm") {
      if (length(parts) <= 2) return(TRUE)
      return(!parts[length(parts)] %in% comp_suffixes)
    }
    TRUE
  }
  avail <- unique(as.character(data$method))
  known <- names(method_labels)
  candidates <- intersect(avail, known)
  candidates <- candidates[vapply(candidates, is_main_plot_method, logical(1))]
  method_order <- method_order[method_order %in% candidates]

  data <- data %>%
    filter(as.character(method) %in% method_order) %>%
    filter(as.character(metric) %in% metric_labels[metric_order]) %>%
    mutate(metric = as.character(metric))

  data$metric_key <- names(metric_labels)[match(data$metric, metric_labels)]

  agg <- data %>%
    group_by(metric, metric_key, method, n) %>%
    summarise(
      lo = compute_lower(value, get_summary_spec(first(metric_key), summary_spec)$range),
      hi = compute_upper(value, get_summary_spec(first(metric_key), summary_spec)$range),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    select(-metric_key)

  agg %>%
    group_by(metric) %>%
    summarise(ymin = min(lo, na.rm = TRUE),
              ymax = max(hi, na.rm = TRUE),
              .groups = "drop")
}


main_ylims <- get_main_plot_ylims(res_plot)




# Translate metric keys to labels in main_ylims so they match the
# computation plot's metric column (which uses labels, not keys).
main_ylims <- main_ylims %>%
  mutate(metric = unname(metric_labels[metric]))


build_computation_plot <- function(data, figure_title = NULL,
                                   metric_order  = default_metric_order,
                                   summary_spec  = metric_summary_spec,
                                   y_limits      = NULL,
                                   ref_comp      = NULL) {

  pm_keys <- unique(as.character(data$method))
  pm_keys <- pm_keys[grepl("^pm_", pm_keys)]
  parsed  = t(sapply(pm_keys, parse_pm_method))
  valid   <- !is.na(parsed[, "family"]) &
             parsed[, "family"]      %in% family_order &
             parsed[, "computation"] %in% computation_order
  pm_keys <- pm_keys[valid]
  parsed  <- parsed[valid, , drop = FALSE]

  if (length(pm_keys) == 0) {
    warning("No PM methods found for computation-comparison plot")
    return(NULL)
  }

  key_to_family <- setNames(parsed[, "family"], pm_keys)
  key_to_comp   <- setNames(parsed[, "computation"], pm_keys)

  data <- data %>%
    filter(as.character(method) %in% pm_keys) %>%
    mutate(
      method      = as.character(method),
      family      = factor(unname(key_to_family[method]), levels = family_order),
      computation = factor(unname(key_to_comp[method]),   levels = computation_order)
    )

  data <- data %>%
    filter(as.character(metric) %in% metric_labels[metric_order]) %>%
    mutate(metric = factor(as.character(metric),
                           levels = metric_labels[metric_order]))

  data$metric_key <- names(metric_labels)[match(as.character(data$metric),
                                                metric_labels)]

  # Reference mode: express each computation as a PAIRED difference from the
  # reference computation (ref_comp, e.g. "exact" = Gauss-Hermite quadrature),
  # within each replicate x n x metric x family. The reference then sits at 0;
  # we shift it back to its own centre below so the panel reads on the metric's
  # natural scale while the whiskers stay the tight paired-difference whiskers.
  rel_mode <- !is.null(ref_comp) && any(as.character(data$computation) == ref_comp)
  if (rel_mode) {
    ref_vals <- data %>%
      filter(as.character(computation) == ref_comp) %>%
      select(iteration, n, metric, metric_key, family, .ref = value)
    data <- data %>%
      inner_join(select(ref_vals, iteration, n, metric, family, .ref),
                 by = c("iteration", "n", "metric", "family")) %>%
      mutate(value = value - .ref) %>%
      select(-.ref)
  }

  agg <- data %>%
    group_by(metric, metric_key, family, computation, n) %>%
    summarise(
      n_sim  = sum(!is.na(value)),
      center = compute_center(value, get_summary_spec(first(metric_key), summary_spec)$center),
      lo     = compute_lower(value, get_summary_spec(first(metric_key), summary_spec)$range),
      hi     = compute_upper(value, get_summary_spec(first(metric_key), summary_spec)$range),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    select(metric, family, computation, n, center, lo, hi)

  # Shift each (metric, family, n) panel up by the reference computation's own
  # centre, so "exact" sits at its true mean/median rather than 0.
  if (rel_mode) {
    ref_center_df <- ref_vals %>%
      group_by(metric, family, n) %>%
      summarise(ref_center = compute_center(
                  .ref, get_summary_spec(first(metric_key), summary_spec)$center),
                .groups = "drop")
    agg <- agg %>%
      left_join(ref_center_df, by = c("metric", "family", "n")) %>%
      mutate(center = center + ref_center,
             lo     = lo + ref_center,
             hi     = hi + ref_center) %>%
      select(-ref_center)
  }

  ref_df <- data.frame(
    metric_key = names(metric_reference),
    yint       = unlist(metric_reference)
  ) %>%
    mutate(metric = factor(metric_labels[metric_key],
                           levels = metric_labels[metric_order])) %>%
    filter(!is.na(metric)) %>%
    select(metric, yint)

  # In reference mode the scale is shifted/differenced, so the absolute main-plot
  # y-limits no longer apply — let panels free-scale to reveal the (small)
  # computation differences.
  agg_anchors <- NULL
  if (!is.null(y_limits) && !rel_mode) {
    families_present <- levels(droplevels(agg$family))
    ns_present       <- unique(agg$n)
    base_grid <- expand.grid(
      metric = unique(agg$metric),
      family = families_present,
      n      = ns_present,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    base_grid <- base_grid %>%
      left_join(y_limits, by = "metric") %>%
      filter(!is.na(ymin), !is.na(ymax))

    agg_anchors <- bind_rows(
      base_grid %>% mutate(center = ymin),
      base_grid %>% mutate(center = ymax)
    ) %>%
      mutate(
        lo          = center,
        hi          = center,
        computation = factor(computation_order[1], levels = computation_order),
        family      = factor(family, levels = family_order),
        metric      = factor(metric, levels = metric_labels[metric_order])
      ) %>%
      select(metric, family, computation, n, center, lo, hi)
  }

  family_labeller <- function(x) family_labels[as.character(x)]
  dodge_width <- 0.6

  p <- ggplot(agg, aes(x = factor(n), y = center,
                       color = computation, shape = computation,
                       group = computation)) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
                  width = 0.3,
                  position = position_dodge(width = dodge_width),
                  linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_point(size = 2,
               position = position_dodge(width = dodge_width)) +
    ggh4x::facet_grid2(
      rows = vars(metric),
      cols = vars(family),
      labeller = labeller(family = family_labeller),
      scales = "free_y",
      switch = "x"  # 1. Moves the column (family) labels to the bottom
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = computation_colors,
                       labels = computation_labels,
                       breaks = computation_order,
                       drop = FALSE, name = "Computation") +
    scale_shape_manual(values = computation_shapes,
                       labels = computation_labels,
                       breaks = computation_order,
                       drop = FALSE, name = "Computation") +
    labs(
      title    = NULL,
      subtitle = if (rel_mode)
        paste0("Whiskers = paired difference vs ", computation_labels[ref_comp],
               " (positioned on the metric's own scale)") else NULL,
      x = "Training sample size",
      y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
    theme(
      legend.position    = "bottom",
      legend.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
      strip.background   = element_rect(fill = "grey92", colour = NA),
      strip.text         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8),
      strip.text.y       = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0),
      strip.placement    = "outside", # 2. Places bottom labels underneath the X-axis numbers
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle      = element_text(colour = "grey35", size = 9),
      axis.text.x        = element_text(size = 8)
    ) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 1),
           shape = guide_legend(nrow = 1))

  if (!is.null(agg_anchors)) {
    p <- p + geom_blank(data = agg_anchors, aes(y = center))
  }

  if (nrow(ref_df) > 0) {
    p <- p + geom_hline(
      data = ref_df,
      aes(yintercept = yint),
      linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4,
      inherit.aes = FALSE
    )
  }

  p
}
```

## NB table
```{r nb-pm-pe-summary}

df_pmpeeff <- data.frame(z=double(), epv=integer(), method=character(), nb=double())
for(z_ in settings$z){
  for(method_ in c("pe","pm")){
    for(n_ in c(500,1000)){
      A <- mean((res |> filter(n==n_ & method %in% paste0(method_, c("_f","_j","_lf","_br")) & metric==paste0("nb",z_)) |> select(value))[[1]])
      df_pmpeeff <- rbind(df_pmpeeff, data.frame(z=z_, n=n_, method=method_, nb=A))
    }
  }
}

nms <- apply(df_pmpeeff, 1, function(x){sprintf("%s|%s|%s", x['z'],x['n'],x['method'])})
rownames(df_pmpeeff) <- gsub(" ", "", nms)

saveRDS(df_pmpeeff, file.path(res_dir,"gusto_pmpeeff.rds"))


# =========================================================================
# Summary: net-benefit difference between PM and PE, by prior (PAIRED)
#
# For each Bayesian prior family (flat / Jeffreys / log-F / Bayesian ridge),
# pm_<prior> and pe_<prior> are evaluated on the SAME resampled data within
# each replicate, so the NB difference pm - pe is PAIRED. We report the mean
# paired difference and its Monte Carlo SE (sd of the per-replicate differences
# / sqrt(n_rep)), by prior, training size (n), and NB threshold (z). Pairing
# isolates the PM-vs-PE effect and gives a much tighter SE than comparing the
# two marginal means. NB only for now; other metrics extend the same way.
# =========================================================================
priors_nb  <- c(f = "Flat", j = "Jeffreys", lf = "log-F", br = "Bayesian ridge")
nb_metrics <- grep("^nb", unique(as.character(res$metric)), value = TRUE)

nb_pm_pe_diff <- res %>%
  filter(as.character(metric) %in% nb_metrics,
         as.character(method) %in% c(paste0("pe_", names(priors_nb)),
                                     paste0("pm_", names(priors_nb)))) %>%
  mutate(method    = as.character(method),
         estimator = ifelse(startsWith(method, "pm_"), "pm", "pe"),
         prior     = sub("^p[me]_", "", method)) %>%
  select(iteration, n, metric, prior, estimator, value) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = estimator, values_from = value) %>%
  filter(!is.na(pm), !is.na(pe)) %>%                 # keep only complete pairs
  mutate(diff = pm - pe) %>%
  group_by(prior, n, metric) %>%
  summarise(
    n_rep          = dplyr::n(),
    mean_pe        = mean(pe),
    se_pe          = sd(pe) / sqrt(n_rep),           # MC SE of mean NB(PE)
    mean_pm        = mean(pm),
    se_pm          = sd(pm) / sqrt(n_rep),           # MC SE of mean NB(PM)
    mean_diff      = mean(diff),                     # mean paired PM - PE
    se_diff        = sd(diff) / sqrt(n_rep),         # MC SE of the mean diff (paired)
    prop_pm_higher = mean(diff > 0),                 # fraction of reps with NB(PM) > NB(PE)
    .groups        = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(prior_label = unname(priors_nb[prior]),
         z           = as.numeric(sub("^nb", "", metric)),
         # % improvement of PM over PE, based on the mean NB. Taken relative to
         # |mean_pe| so the sign stays meaningful when NB is negative (for
         # mean_pe > 0 this is just the usual (pm - pe)/pe). Special case: if PE
         # is non-beneficial (mean_pe <= 0) but PM is beneficial (mean_pm > 0),
         # PM turns a useless/harmful model into a useful one -> report Inf.
         # A zero PE baseline with non-positive PM is undefined -> NA.
         pct_improvement = dplyr::case_when(
           mean_pe <= 0 & mean_pm > 0 ~ Inf,
           mean_pe == 0               ~ NA_real_,
           TRUE                       ~ 100 * (mean_pm - mean_pe) / abs(mean_pe)
         )) %>%
  arrange(match(prior, names(priors_nb)), n, z) %>%
  select(prior, prior_label, n, z, n_rep, mean_pe, se_pe, mean_pm, se_pm,
         mean_diff, se_diff, prop_pm_higher, pct_improvement)

# (The PM-vs-doubling-n comparison and its bootstrap CI were removed; the
# posterior-mean gain is now expressed via the equivalent sample size n*,
# computed below.) nb_pm_pe_diff is complete above.
saveRDS(nb_pm_pe_diff, file = file.path(res_dir, "gusto_nb_pm_pe_diff.rds"))

# --- Learning-curve n*: PE training size matching PM's net benefit ---------
# NB_inf is the candidate model's net-benefit CEILING, estimated directly by
# fitting the candidate model to the FULL cohort and evaluating it there with
# the same (standardized) net-benefit formula used in the simulation. Because
# the priors are negligible at this sample size, this single MLE fit is the
# shared asymptote for all priors (and PE = PM in the limit), so NB_inf depends
# only on the threshold z, not the prior. NOTE: the simulation reports
# STANDARDIZED NB (raw NB divided by prevalence); NB_inf must use the SAME scale,
# so we divide by the population prevalence here too.
reg_pop  <- glm(settings$fm_model, data = df_final, family = binomial())
p_pop    <- predict(reg_pop, newdata = df_final, type = "response")
prev_pop <- mean(df_final$Y)
nb_inf_tbl <- data.frame(
  z      = settings$z,
  nb_inf = vapply(settings$z, function(zz) {
    nb_term <- df_final$Y - (1 - df_final$Y) * zz / (1 - zz)
    nb0     <- max(0, mean(nb_term))
    (mean((p_pop > zz) * nb_term - nb0)) / prev_pop   # standardized NB, matching the sim scale
  }, numeric(1))
)
saveRDS(nb_inf_tbl, file.path(res_dir, "gusto_nb_inf.rds"))

nb_pm_pe_diff <- nb_pm_pe_diff %>% left_join(nb_inf_tbl, by = "z")

# Inverse-power learning curve (Figueroa): NB(n) = NB_inf - b * n^c.
# With NB_inf fixed (above), the decay exponent c is the slope of
#   log(NB_inf - NB_PE(n)) = log b + c * log n
# fit over the three sizes per (prior, z). Guard: if a cell's c is >= 0 or
# non-finite (MC noise on 3 points), fall back to c = -1 (the 1/n excess-risk
# rate for a parametric model).
c_fit <- nb_pm_pe_diff %>%
  group_by(prior, z) %>%
  summarise(c_exp = {
      g <- nb_inf - mean_pe                       # gap to ceiling at each n
      ok <- is.finite(g) & g > 0
      if (sum(ok) >= 2) unname(coef(lm(log(g[ok]) ~ log(n[ok])))[2]) else NA_real_
    }, .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(c_exp = ifelse(is.finite(c_exp) & c_exp < 0, c_exp, -1))

# n* = anchored power-law regret ratio: PE's curve forced through its OBSERVED
# point at n0 with exponent c, so
#   n* = n0 * [ (NB_inf - NB_PM(n0)) / (NB_inf - NB_PE(n0)) ]^(1/c).
# Reduces to n0 * (NB_inf - NB_PE) / (NB_inf - NB_PM) when c = -1, and is
# sign-consistent with ΔNB for any c < 0 (n* > n0 iff PM beats PE at n0).
nb_pm_pe_diff <- nb_pm_pe_diff %>%
  left_join(c_fit, by = c("prior", "z")) %>%
  mutate(nstar = dplyr::case_when(
                   (nb_inf - mean_pm) <= 0 ~ Inf,        # PM at/above ceiling
                   (nb_inf - mean_pe) <= 0 ~ NA_real_,   # PE at/above ceiling at n0 (noise)
                   TRUE ~ n * ((nb_inf - mean_pm) / (nb_inf - mean_pe))^(1 / c_exp)))

# --- Clean manuscript table -----------------------------------------------
# Thresholds become columns (wide format); SEs dropped for readability.
# Rows: prior x n, sorted by prior. The four priors carry the full PE / PM /
# ΔNB / n* comparison. The two single-prediction comparators (frequentist ridge
# = plug-in only; MCMC ridge = posterior mean only) have NO PE-vs-PM pair, so
# only one of PE/PM is filled and ΔNB / n* are left empty (NA -> blank); they
# sit at the bottom of the table.

nb_zvals   <- sort(unique(nb_pm_pe_diff$z))
nb_zlabels <- sprintf("z=%.2f", nb_zvals)

# Single-prediction comparators: one NB each, placed in PE (plug-in ridge) or
# PM (posterior-mean MCMC ridge); the other estimate, ΔNB and n* stay NA.
comparator_methods <- c(pe_ridge_min = "Ridge (CV-min)",
                        pm_br_mcmc   = "Bayesian ridge (MCMC)")
comp_long <- res %>%
  filter(as.character(metric) %in% nb_metrics,
         as.character(method) %in% names(comparator_methods),
         !is.na(value)) %>%
  mutate(method = as.character(method),
         z      = as.numeric(sub("^nb", "", metric))) %>%
  group_by(method, n, z) %>%
  summarise(mean_nb = mean(value), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(prior_label = unname(comparator_methods[method]),
         mean_pe   = ifelse(startsWith(method, "pe_"), mean_nb, NA_real_),
         mean_pm   = ifelse(startsWith(method, "pm_"), mean_nb, NA_real_),
         mean_diff = NA_real_,
         nstar     = NA_real_) %>%
  select(prior_label, n, z, mean_pe, mean_pm, mean_diff, nstar)

# Prior ordering: the four priors first (priors_nb order), comparators last.
prior_label_levels <- c(unname(priors_nb), unname(comparator_methods))

nb_long <- bind_rows(
  nb_pm_pe_diff %>% select(prior_label, n, z, mean_pe, mean_pm, mean_diff, nstar),
  comp_long
) %>%
  mutate(prior_label = factor(prior_label, levels = prior_label_levels)) %>%
  arrange(n, prior_label, z)

nb_table <- nb_long %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    id_cols     = c(n, prior_label),
    names_from  = z,
    values_from = c(mean_pe, mean_pm, mean_diff, nstar),
    names_glue  = "{.value}__{z}"
  ) %>%
  arrange(n, prior_label)

# Re-order columns: n, Prior, then per threshold PE / PM / ΔNB / n*
ordered_cols <- c("n", "prior_label")
for (zv in nb_zvals) {
  ordered_cols <- c(ordered_cols,
    paste0("mean_pe__",   zv),
    paste0("mean_pm__",   zv),
    paste0("mean_diff__", zv),
    paste0("nstar__",     zv))
}
nb_table <- nb_table[, ordered_cols]

# Round NB-scale columns to 4 dp; n* to nearest integer (NA stays NA -> blank)
num_cols   <- setdiff(colnames(nb_table), c("n", "prior_label"))
nstar_cols <- grep("^nstar__", num_cols, value = TRUE)
other_cols <- setdiff(num_cols, nstar_cols)
nb_table[, other_cols] <- lapply(nb_table[, other_cols], function(x) round(x, 4))
nb_table[, nstar_cols] <- lapply(nb_table[, nstar_cols], function(x) round(x, 0))

kable(nb_table,
      col.names = c("Prior", "n",
                    rep(c("PE", "PM", "ΔNB", "n*"), length(nb_zvals))),
      caption   = "GUSTO: net benefit by prior and training size, with PE-equivalent sample size n* (frequentist and MCMC ridge are single-prediction comparators)")

saveRDS(list(nb_table = nb_table, zvals = nb_zvals, zlabels = nb_zlabels),
        file = file.path(res_dir, "gusto_nb_table.rds"))
```
